# ClipMenu Swift parity progress - 2026-06-19

This note records implementation progress toward `doc/feature_test_cases.md`; it is not a substitute for a full manual matrix run.

## Strengthened areas

- Action decoding now normalizes legacy action dictionaries at runtime and in Preferences, including missing `type` inference and `removeAction` normalization.
- Excluded application defaults now tolerate Objective-C bridged dictionaries in both clipboard capture and Recording Preferences.
- Legacy `clips.data` migration now reads string, RTF/RTFD, PDF, filenames, URL, TIFF, and PICT data from legacy pasteboard-type archive keys, including the older NeXT/Apple pasteboard type names used by Objective-C archives.
- JavaScript action execution now restores the previous frontmost app on every runner exit path after `ClipMenu.activate()` or JavaScript dialogs.
- RTF/RTFD and URL clips keep a plain string fallback when available for titles and action payloads, while action-menu filtering still follows the original stored pasteboard-type rules.
- Direct modifier-click action mappings now preserve Objective-C's separate sender-tag dispatch path instead of using the action-menu applicability prefilter; when a configured dictionary behavior is present, selection is consumed even if the invoked action ultimately no-ops for that legacy target.
- A new Debug-only modified-click verifier (`debugWriteModifiedClickBehaviorReportAfterLaunchDelay`) now covers the remaining interaction branches around CM-ACT-007, CM-ACT-008, and CM-ACT-009 without depending on external UI automation. In an isolated run, a Shift-modified selection with `Enable Action = false` preserved the normal clip-selection fallback (`disabledActionsPasteboard = "Styled Input"`, clip count stayed `1`), proving disabled actions do not swallow ordinary paste selection. The same report then switched to `controlClickBehavior = "popUpActionMenu"` plus `Invoke action immediately = true` and a single-action `actions.plist` containing only `Remove`; a simulated Control/right-click selection removed the clip immediately (`immediateActionClipCountAfter = 0`) without first writing the clip text to the pasteboard. Finally, direct Shift/Option/Command mappings were exercised through the real `selectClip` path with tracked popup-modifier flags: Shift-triggered `Remove` dropped the clip count to `0`, Option-triggered `Paste as Plain Text` wrote `"Styled Input"`, and Command-triggered bundled `UPPERCASE.js` wrote `"STYLED INPUT"`, with `modifiedClickBehaviorMatchesExpected = true`. That materially strengthens the remaining proof around modifier-based action dispatch parity.
- Paste as Plain Text and JavaScript actions now require the stored String pasteboard type, matching the original `CMIsPerformableAction` filtering instead of enabling from fallback text alone.
- Hotkey registration now refuses invalid negative key codes instead of clamping them to `A`, preserving the original empty/disabled combo behavior for corrupted or partially migrated defaults.
- Default registration now preserves the original `hotKeys` dictionary and legacy `actions` placeholder alongside the modern split hotkey keys and `actions.plist` store, so clean/imported defaults keep the Objective-C domain shape while the Swift UI uses modern controls.
- A fresh isolated June 27, 2026 clean-home defaults-shape verifier (`debugWriteDefaultsShapeReportAfterLaunchDelay`) now turns that registration-shape note into direct runtime evidence too. Launching the current Debug build with an empty temp home produced `legacyHotKeysMatchExpected = true`, `legacyActionsMatchExpected = true`, `modernSplitHotKeysMatchExpected = true`, `persistentDefaultsContainLegacyHotKeys = false`, `persistentDefaultsContainLegacyActions = false`, `actionsPlistExists = false`, and `matchesExpected = true`. Concretely, the app surfaced the original Objective-C compatibility defaults through registered values before any user data existed: `hotKeys` still exposed the legacy `ClipMenu` / `HistoryMenu` / `SnippetsMenu` dictionary, `actions` still exposed the old `[{ name = removeAction, path = "" }]` placeholder, and the modern split hotkey keys simultaneously resolved to the expected visible/runtime defaults. That gives direct evidence that the Swift app still presents the old defaults-domain shape for clean launches while keeping the newer `actions.plist` store path and split hotkey controls.
- Verified the modern snippet editor preserves the original title/content guard: empty names are rejected by normalization, and a newly titled snippet with empty content receives the title as its content.
- A focused Debug-only snippet-normalization verifier (`debugWriteSnippetNormalizationReportAfterLaunchDelay`) now gives direct runtime evidence for the remaining title/content defaulting quirk instead of relying on code inspection alone. In a fresh isolated June 27, 2026 run, retitling an empty default snippet to `Greeting` produced `{title: "Greeting", content: "Greeting"}`, leaving the title at the default `untitled snippet` preserved empty content, and renaming a snippet that already had body text preserved that existing content. The report ended with `matchesExpected = true`, materially strengthening `CM-SNIP-005`.
- Quit-time history persistence still runs early enough to report save failures, but the failure alert now matches the Objective-C app's single-`OK` error surface and does not add a Swift-only cancel-quit branch.
- A new Debug-only quit-menu verifier (`debugWriteQuitMenuItemReportAfterLaunchDelay`) now gives `CM-LAUNCH-003` direct runtime evidence instead of relying on older manual runs that predated later termination-path cleanup. In a fresh isolated June 27, 2026 run, the harness built the real main status menu, resolved `Quit ClipMenu` to `target = NSApplication` and `action = terminate:`, invoked that menu item's action, and recorded the live delegate path before the process exited. The resulting report landed with `quitItemFound = true`, `quitItemTargetIsApplication = true`, `attemptedSendAction = true`, `applicationShouldTerminateCalled = true`, `applicationWillTerminateCalled = true`, `terminationPersistenceHandledAtWillTerminate = true`, `fallbackTriggered = false`, and `matchesExpected = true`. That materially strengthens `CM-LAUNCH-003` and also confirms the current Swift build no longer reproduces the earlier “Quit ClipMenu did not terminate” manual failure note.
- Verified clipboard history trimming keeps the newest sorted prefix, matching the original controller's removal of overflow clips from the end of the sorted history.
- A new Debug-only history-selection verifier (`debugWriteHistorySelectionReportAfterLaunchDelay`) now proves the menu-title versus paste payload split directly for text history items. In a fresh isolated run with paste synthesis disabled, selecting a multiline clip produced `multilineTitle = "1. line one"` while writing the full `"line one\nline two"` string to the pasteboard, and selecting a long clip produced `longTitle = "1. This is a very lo..."` while preserving the complete original text on the pasteboard. The same report also showed the tooltip path still exposes the unclipped multiline content and applies the configured length cap to long text (`longTooltip` truncated at the requested 80 characters), strengthening CM-HIST-005, CM-HIST-006, and CM-TYPE-010 evidence without relying on manual UI inspection.
- Runtime snippet menu items now preserve the original snippet-specific numbering behavior, lack of numeric key equivalents, and always-on full-content tooltips.
- JavaScript action resolution now recovers relative user action paths under `script/action` from Application Support while preserving bundled action path priority for saved bundled/default actions.
- Clipboard capture now rejects enabled-but-empty pasteboard payloads after extraction, preventing blank history rows for empty text or malformed advertised pasteboard types.
- Controlled isolated verification now covers more of that capture gate directly through the app-level clipboard-selection helper: a scratch pasteboard advertising only unsupported `public.html` data is ignored, enabled-but-empty string payloads are ignored, a plain-text payload is ignored when the `String` store type is disabled, and a plain-text payload is rejected when the injected frontmost bundle id matches the excluded-app list but accepted for a non-excluded bundle id. The latest extension of that same isolated clip-store smoke now also proves broader record-type filtering directly: with every `storeTypes` entry disabled, both plain-text and PDF scratch pasteboards are rejected (`allDisabledStoreTypesRejectString = true`, `allDisabledStoreTypesRejectPDF = true`); with a PDF-only configuration the runtime still rejects plain text while accepting a generated PDF payload (`pdfOnlyStoreTypesRejectString = true`, `pdfOnlyStoreTypesAcceptPDF = true`); with an RTF-only configuration it rejects plain text while still capturing styled RTF plus the legacy string fallback (`rtfOnlyStoreTypesRejectString = true`, `rtfOnlyStoreTypesAcceptRTF = true`); and with `RTFD` disabled a pasteboard carrying only `NSRTFDPboardType` is rejected outright (`disabledRTFDTypeRejected = true`). That materially strengthens `CM-PREF-003`, `CM-TYPE-001`, and the rich-text side of `CM-TYPE-002` without touching live user state.
- Re-ran that broader isolated clip-store roundtrip verifier on June 27, 2026 against the current Debug build and harvested several still-missing history/runtime branches from one clean temp-home pass. The same report again showed unsupported advertised data was ignored (`unsupportedTypeRejected = true`), excluded-app capture was blocked while a non-excluded bundle id still captured (`excludedAppRejected = true`, `nonExcludedAppAccepted = true`), and reorder-after-paste preserved the original Objective-C split: with `reorderClipsAfterPasting = true`, selecting `select-alpha` moved it to the top (`reorderEnabledMovedSelectionToTop = true`), while disabling the preference left `["select-gamma", "select-beta", "select-alpha"]` unchanged after selecting `select-beta` (`reorderDisabledPreservedOrder = true`). That materially strengthens `CM-HIST-007`, `CM-HIST-008`, `CM-HIST-009`, and `CM-HIST-010`.
- A new Debug-only plain-text capture verifier (`debugWritePlainTextCaptureReportAfterLaunchDelay`) now gives `CM-HIST-001` its own direct runtime proof instead of leaving it implied by larger clip-store smoke. In a fresh June 27, 2026 run, a scratch pasteboard carrying only `alpha` flowed through the app's real `capturedClip(from:)` helper, produced a stored clip with primary type `public.utf8-plain-text`, and rendered a History menu with the single visible title `["1. alpha"]`. The final report landed at `capturedExists = true`, `capturedText = "alpha"`, `orderedTexts = ["alpha"]`, and `matchesExpected = true`.
- Clip replay now declares and writes only the stored legacy pasteboard types, matching the original `copyClipToPasteboard:` behavior instead of adding modern `public.url` or file-url object flavors during replay.
- A new Debug-only typed-clip rendering verifier (`debugWriteTypedClipRenderingReportAfterLaunchDelay`) now covers the visible menu treatment for representative PDF, file-path, and URL clips instead of proving only pasteboard round-tripping. In a fresh June 27, 2026 run, a generated PDF clip rendered as `1. (PDF)` with an icon and empty tooltip, a Finder-style file clip rendered as `2. (Filenames)` with an icon and empty tooltip while preserving `["/tmp/clipmenu-debug-file.txt"]` internally, and a URL clip rendered as `3. https://example.com/clipmenu-debug` with both an icon and the full URL tooltip while preserving `["https://example.com/clipmenu-debug"]` in the stored URL payload. The report ended with `matchesExpected = true`, materially strengthening `CM-TYPE-003`, `CM-TYPE-004`, and `CM-TYPE-005`.
- Menu thumbnails are now limited to actual image pasteboard types, so non-image clips with image-like data fall back to their configured file-type icons like the original menu renderer.
- Image clip menu items now preserve the original renderer's icon-suppression quirk: when an image payload exists and `showImageInTheMenu` is off, Swift no longer falls through to the TIFF/PICT file-type icon, while failed thumbnail generation with image display enabled can still fall back to the configured icon. The latest isolated clip-store smoke now proves both the capture and presentation halves directly: with a TIFF-only `storeTypes` configuration the runtime rejects plain text but accepts a generated TIFF payload (`tiffOnlyStoreTypesRejectString = true`, `tiffOnlyStoreTypesAcceptImage = true`), and with `TIFF` disabled the same image-only pasteboard is rejected (`disabledTIFFTypeRejected = true`). On the menu-rendering side, `showImageInTheMenu = true` plus `thumbnailWidth = 4` / `thumbnailHeight = 6` produced a real bounded thumbnail (`showImageEnabledHasThumbnail = true`, `showImageEnabledThumbnailFitsBounds = true`), while `showImageInTheMenu = false` suppressed the image clip's menu image entirely (`showImageDisabledSuppressesImageClipImage = true`) and a non-image PDF clip still received its ordinary file-type icon when menu icons remained enabled (`nonImageClipStillUsesIconWhenIconsEnabled = true`). That materially strengthens `CM-TYPE-006` and `CM-TYPE-007`.
- That same isolated menu-image smoke now also covers the explicit icon-size branch for non-image clips, materially strengthening `CM-TYPE-009`: with `showIconInTheMenu = true`, the same PDF menu item resized to exact `16x16`, `32x32`, and `48x48` icon sizes as `menuIconSize` changed (`menuIconSize16MatchesExpected = true`, `menuIconSize32MatchesExpected = true`, `menuIconSize48MatchesExpected = true`), and with `showIconInTheMenu = false` the non-image icon disappeared again (`menuIconsDisabledSuppressesNonImageIcon = true`). That keeps the Objective-C-sized icon policy intact while the modern SwiftUI preferences surface drives the setting.
- The Updates preferences pane now follows the original Preferences nib's availability rules instead of a looser Swift-only interpretation: when `Automatically check for updates` is off, the interval popup, `Include pre-releases`, and `Check Now` are all disabled together. This matches the installed Objective-C nib bindings for controls `1337`, `1350`, `1425`, and `1330`, rather than treating manual update checks as always available from that pane.
- A fresh isolated June 27, 2026 rerun of a new Debug self-report (`debugWriteUpdatePreferencesAvailabilityReportAfterLaunchDelay`) now turns that Updates-pane availability note into direct runtime evidence too. With the Preferences window opened directly on the `Updates` pane in a clean temp-home launch, the report showed `disabledState = { preReleasesEnabled: false, automaticallyInstallUpdatesEnabled: false, intervalEnabled: false, checkNowEnabled: false }` when `Automatically check for updates` was off, then `enabledState = { preReleasesEnabled: true, automaticallyInstallUpdatesEnabled: true, intervalEnabled: true, checkNowEnabled: true }` once automatic checks were on and the feed URL was present, plus `checkingState.checkNowEnabled = false` while a manual check was notionally in progress. The final report landed with `automaticChecksOffDisablesDependentControls = true`, `automaticChecksOnEnablesDependentControlsWhenFeedPresent = true`, `checkingStateDisablesCheckNow = true`, and `matchesExpected = true`, materially strengthening the control-surface half of `CM-PREF-010`.
- The modern Updates pane now presents that same Objective-C-compatible behavior with a cleaner Swift surface instead of a single dense control row. Feed/channel state and checking state now appear as compact status badges beside the existing controls, the last-check timestamp uses a steadier monospaced presentation, and `Check Now` is surfaced as an icon-backed action button while preserving the same enable/disable rules. A fresh isolated June 27, 2026 rerun of `debugWriteUpdatePreferencesAvailabilityReportAfterLaunchDelay` stayed fully green after the UI pass (`automaticChecksOffDisablesDependentControls = true`, `automaticChecksOnEnablesDependentControlsWhenFeedPresent = true`, `checkingStateDisablesCheckNow = true`, `matchesExpected = true`), so the visual refresh did not loosen the original preferences semantics.
- The Updates pane now also opens with a clearer top-level summary of update state instead of dropping straight into checkbox rows. The Swift shell now calls out whether checks are automatic or manual-only, which feed family is active, and the current interval before the user drills into the stored Sparkle-style controls, while preserving the same enable/disable matrix and progress-window behavior underneath. Fresh isolated June 27, 2026 reruns stayed green immediately after that shell pass: `debugWriteUpdatePreferencesAvailabilityReportAfterLaunchDelay` again returned `automaticChecksOffDisablesDependentControls = true`, `automaticChecksOnEnablesDependentControlsWhenFeedPresent = true`, `checkingStateDisablesCheckNow = true`, and `matchesExpected = true`; and `debugWriteCheckingForUpdatesReportAfterLaunchDelay` again showed `windowTitle = "Checking for updates..."`, `cancelButtonTitle = "Cancel"`, `hasProgressIndicator = true`, `isVisibleWhileShown = true`, and `styleMaskContainsTitled = true`.
- A companion June 27, 2026 Updates-surface report now also captures the live pane contract directly through the SwiftUI preferences layer (`debugWriteUpdatesPreferencesReportAfterLaunchDelay`). In an isolated launch forced onto the `Updates` tab, the report wrote `title = "Preferences"`, `toolbarStyle = "preference"`, and a `paneSnapshot` with `paneTitle = "Updates"`, section titles `["Updates", "Status"]`, restored control titles `["Automatically check for updates:", "Include pre-releases", "Automatically download and install updates in the future", "Time interval", "Check Now"]`, interval titles `["Daily", "Weekly", "Monthly"]`, and the modern overview title `Software Update Behavior`. The same snapshot also recorded the live launch-state summary exported by the pane: `overviewBadges = ["Automatic checks on", "Stable", "Daily"]`, `overviewDetail = "Automatic checks, channel selection, and install behavior follow the same Sparkle-style rules as the original app."`, plus state values `automaticChecks = true`, `preReleases = false`, `automaticallyInstallUpdates = false`, `interval = 86400`, `hasFeedURL = true`, `isChecking = false`, and `lastCheckedDisplay = "Never"`. That gives direct pane-level runtime evidence for the modernized Updates surface instead of relying only on the separate availability and updater-flow probes.
- The transient `Checking for updates...` progress window now also keeps the old updater contract while looking more at home beside the newer Swift surfaces. The app still presents a floating titled panel with a live indeterminate progress bar and `Cancel`, but the content now uses the app icon, clearer status copy, and less cramped spacing instead of the older bare utility panel layout. A fresh isolated June 27, 2026 rerun of `debugWriteCheckingForUpdatesReportAfterLaunchDelay` confirmed the surface stayed behaviorally intact after the refresh: `windowTitle = "Checking for updates..."`, `contentTitle = "Checking for updates..."`, `contentDetail = "ClipMenu is checking the current update feed."`, `cancelButtonTitle = "Cancel"`, `hasProgressIndicator = true`, `isVisibleWhileShown = true`, `levelIsFloating = true`, and `styleMaskContainsTitled = true`.
- The updater result alerts now also carry more of that modernized Swift presentation instead of reserving the visual refresh only for the progress panel. The `Update Available` and `Ready to Install` alerts now attach compact accessory summary cards with the app icon plus clearer state copy, while still preserving the same Sparkle-era titles, informative text, button ordering, and skip/install behavior. Fresh isolated June 27, 2026 reruns of both updater alert reports stayed green after the UI pass: `debugWriteAvailableUpdateAlertReportAfterLaunchDelay` still returned `messageText = "Update Available"`, `buttonTitles = ["Install Update", "Skip This Version", "Later"]`, `buttonOrderMatchesExpected = true`, `primaryButtonMatchesSparkle = true`, and `hasAccessoryView = true`, while `debugWriteReadyToInstallUpdateReportAfterLaunchDelay` still returned `messageText = "Ready to Install"`, `buttonTitles = ["Install and Relaunch", "Later"]`, `installOpenedExpectedFile = true`, `laterDidNotOpenFile = true`, and now also `hasAccessoryView = true`.
- The remaining passive updater alerts now use that same accessory-card treatment too, so the custom Swift updater no longer falls back to plain stock panels after the richer progress and result surfaces. `Failed to Check for Updates`, `Failed to Download Update`, and `You're up to date!` now keep their original titles, informative text, and single `OK` dismissal while adding the same icon-led summary card and steadier explanatory copy used elsewhere in the updater flow. A fresh isolated June 27, 2026 run of the new `debugWriteUpdatePassiveAlertsReportAfterLaunchDelay` verifier confirmed the behavior stayed legacy-compatible after the refresh: the report returned `checkFailureMessageText = "Failed to Check for Updates"`, `downloadFailureMessageText = "Failed to Download Update"`, `upToDateMessageText = "You're up to date!"`, all three button arrays remained `["OK"]`, each alert reported `HasAccessoryView = true`, and `matchesExpected = true`.
- Update bundle metadata now restores the original `SUPublicDSAKeyFile` declaration, and the built `dsa_pub.pem` matches the key bundled in `/Applications/ClipMenu.app`.
- Release bundle identity now matches the installed Objective-C app's visible metadata: `ClipMenu.app`, bundle identifier `com.naotaka.ClipMenu`, version/build `0.4.3`, original `ClipMenu` icon key, `LSUIElement = 1`, and the 2008-2009 copyright string.
- Update last-check state now uses Sparkle's legacy `SULastCheckTime` defaults key, and automatic fallback checks no longer open the appcast URL in a browser.
- Action and snippet file-store saves now show visible error alerts with the underlying system error instead of silently swallowing failed writes.
- Verified the legacy Action Preferences Add button always appends reserved actions at the root end; the Swift editor already matches that behavior, with nested placement handled by drag and drop.
- Re-ran the Action Preferences tree timing verifier on June 27, 2026 against the current Debug build to turn that Add-button note into direct runtime evidence. With the action tree seeded as `Folder -> First Child, Second Child` plus a top-level `Tail Action`, selecting reserved `Remove` and invoking the same Add path produced `addSelectedReservedActionPaths = ["Folder", "Folder/First Child", "Folder/Second Child", "Tail Action", "Remove"]` and `addSelectedReservedActionMatchesExpected = true`, confirming the Swift editor still appends newly added reserved actions at the root end exactly like the installed Objective-C app.
- History submenu range titles now use the full sorted history count like Objective-C `_makeSubmenuItemWithCount`, even when `maxHistorySize` limits visible clips, while preserving zero-based and one-based numbering behavior.
- The main menu `Clear History` command remains enabled when history is empty, matching the Objective-C status menu's always-enabled command item instead of adding a Swift-only disabled state.
- The feature test matrix now records that main-status-menu `Clear History` stays enabled after clearing, so future parity runs follow the installed Objective-C `MenuController` behavior instead of the stricter `AppController` validation path.
- A new Debug-only clear-history command verifier (`debugWriteClearHistoryMenuReportAfterLaunchDelay`) now gives that visible command behavior its own direct runtime proof instead of relying on older manual release notes plus the separate suppression/pathology checks. In a fresh isolated June 27, 2026 run, the seeded main menu began with visible history items plus `Clear History`, confirmed the command was enabled before invocation, cleared `["clear-menu-two", "clear-menu-one"]` through the real `performClearHistory` path, and then rebuilt the main menu with no history items while leaving `Clear History` enabled. The final report landed at `clearHistorySucceeded = true`, `clearHistoryEnabledBefore = true`, `clearHistoryEnabledAfter = true`, and `matchesExpected = true`, materially strengthening `CM-PASTE-010`.
- A new Debug-only clear-history suppression verifier (`debugWriteClearHistorySuppressionReportAfterLaunchDelay`) now covers the remaining confirmation-suppression branch directly. A fresh isolated run under a temporary `CFFIXED_USER_HOME` seeded two clips, confirmed the first clear with suppression enabled, and then added a third clip before invoking clear again through a resolver that would have cancelled if a second confirmation were still required. The report showed `initialTexts = ["clear-two", "clear-one"]`, `afterFirstTexts = []`, `alertDisabledAfterSuppression = true`, `beforeSecondTexts = ["clear-three"]`, `secondInvocationCleared = true`, `afterSecondTexts = []`, and `suppressionFlowMatchesExpected = true`, confirming CM-PASTE-011 parity with the installed Objective-C app's persisted "do not ask again" behavior.
- The default Action menu now matches the original Objective-C default (`Paste as Plain Text`, `Case`, `Trim`, `Remove`) while keeping additional built-in and bundled actions available from Preferences.
- A new Debug-only action-behavior verifier (`debugWriteActionBehaviorReportAfterLaunchDelay`) now covers the core action filtering and built-in invocation paths directly against the live runtime action menu. Using an isolated temp home and a fixture `actions.plist` with `Paste as Plain Text`, `Paste as File Path`, `Paste as HFS File Path`, bundled `UPPERCASE.js`, and `Remove`, the latest run showed string-like clip and snippet targets expose `["Paste as Plain Text", "UPPERCASE.js", "Remove"]` while file targets expose `["Paste as File Path", "Paste as HFS File Path", "Remove"]`, proving the menu no longer leaks file-path actions onto text targets or JavaScript/plain-text actions onto filename-only clips. The same report also verified live built-in execution through `selectAction`: plain-text conversion wrote `"Styled Input"` to the pasteboard, POSIX file-path conversion wrote `"/tmp/example-a.txt\n/tmp/example-b.txt"`, HFS conversion wrote `Macintosh HD:private:tmp:...` paths, and `Remove` dropped the clip count from `1` to `0`. That materially strengthens CM-ACT-002 through CM-ACT-006 evidence without depending on manual UI scripting.
- Re-ran that Debug action-behavior verifier on June 27, 2026 against the current Debug build to make the remaining action-menu matrix items explicit. The fresh report again landed with `actionBehaviorMatchesExpected = true`, showed live action-menu availability for text, snippet, and file targets (`textActionTitles = ["Paste as Plain Text", "UPPERCASE.js", "Remove"]`, `snippetActionTitles = ["Paste as Plain Text", "UPPERCASE.js", "Remove"]`, `fileActionTitles = ["Paste as File Path", "Paste as HFS File Path", "Remove"]`), and reconfirmed the built-in invocation outputs (`plainTextPasteboard = "Styled Input"`, `posixPasteboard = "/tmp/example-a.txt\n/tmp/example-b.txt"`, `hfsPasteboard = "Macintosh HD:private:tmp:example-a.txt\nMacintosh HD:private:tmp:example-b.txt"`, `removeCountAfter = 0`). In a fresh isolated June 27, 2026 run with an overridden support directory, the harness seeded a user `script/action` fixture in a deliberately non-alphabetized creation order, then compared the live reserved-action tree against an independent raw `contentsOfDirectory` walk using the same localized title mapping the app applies. The report landed with `userMatchesFilesystemEnumeration = true` and `bundledMatchesFilesystemEnumeration = true`, and preserved the exact raw traversal order instead of a title sort in both cases: the user fixture came back as `["Alpha Folder", "Alpha Folder/Omega Script", "Middle Script", "Beta Folder", "Beta Folder/Alpha Script", "Beta Folder/Zeta Script", "Last Script"]`, while the bundled tree began `["Reverse", "Collapse Spaces", "Japanese", ... , "Case", "Case/lowercase", "Case/Capitalize", "Case/Title Case", "Case/UPPERCASE"]`. That upgrades the discovery-order note from an implementation claim to runtime-verified parity for the reserved browser and action insertion source.
- Verified a real Objective-C `actions.plist` decodes with the Swift action model and all saved bundled/user JavaScript action paths resolve through the migrated resource and Application Support lookup rules.
- Swift-written `actions.plist` leaf nodes now omit the `children` key, matching Objective-C `BaseNode` dictionary serialization while preserving folder children and the legacy decoder's tolerance for either shape.
- Missing JavaScript action files now show the original top-level "The script you selected does not exist" alert while retaining migrated-path recovery; unreadable resolved scripts keep the deeper "Unable to load script" / "Your script file does not exist." loader alert.
- JavaScript action rich-text font attributes now reject missing or nonpositive font sizes like the original `NSFont fontWithName:size:` path instead of substituting a modern system size.
- JavaScript action rich-text color parsing now follows the original `NSColor+String` whitespace behavior: named and hex colors are not pre-trimmed, and CSS `rgb`/`rgba` parsing trims whitespace but not newline characters.
- JavaScript action parse/setup failures now use the original "Script Error" / "Failed to evaluate script" alert, while runtime exceptions still use "Script Exception Raised".
- `ClipMenu.require` now follows the original `pathExtension == "js"` behavior and returns `false` for nil or empty filenames before searching user then bundled libraries.
- The JavaScript bridge now matches the Objective-C namespace and wrapper flow more closely: scripts run under a local `try/catch` that fills `__scriptException`, `ClipMenu.require` searches only user then bundled lib folders, and the Swift-only `CM` alias is no longer injected.
- The SwiftUI Preferences window now uses a native macOS sidebar selection model and exposes `Shortcuts` as its own pane instead of burying hotkeys inside `General`, keeping the legacy settings while making the modern UI match the acceptance surface more closely.
- The modern Action preferences pane now keeps the original modifier-click behavior choices and enable-action gating while using an adaptive grid, so the controls remain readable in narrower Preferences windows.
- The Japanese localization now covers the main modern SwiftUI Preferences, Snippet Editor, accessibility, and update-check labels introduced by the migration, reducing mixed English/Japanese UI while preserving the original localized legacy strings.
- A fresh June 27, 2026 localization pass now extends that Japanese coverage deeper into the modern Preferences shell and summary surfaces that had still been leaking English after the UI refreshes. `Japanese.lproj/Localizable.strings` now includes translations for newer sidebar summaries, pane overview badges, Action/Shortcuts/Type/Updates summary copy, snippet-position summaries, and visible status phrases such as `Actions On`, `Menu bar utility`, `Software Update Behavior`, and `Delete clears a shortcut`, while also restoring the visible `Edit Snippets...` command to Japanese. A follow-up scan over `NSLocalizedString` literals in `Source/SwiftUINativeWindows.swift` and `Source/AppController.swift` reduced the remaining missing-key count in the Japanese bundle from `318` to `220`, and both `plutil -lint Japanese.lproj/Localizable.strings` and `xcodebuild -project ClipMenu.xcodeproj -scheme ClipMenu -configuration Debug build` stayed green. That does not finish localization parity, but it materially reduces mixed-language Swift UI in the most visible modern settings surfaces.
- Two more focused June 27, 2026 follow-up passes pushed that same Japanese fallback count down further, from `220` to `170` and then to `140`, again with `plutil -lint Japanese.lproj/Localizable.strings` and `xcodebuild -project ClipMenu.xcodeproj -scheme ClipMenu -configuration Debug build` both staying green after each batch. Those passes specifically filled in more first-viewport modern UI copy across the refreshed Preferences panes: type/icon summaries (`File Extension`, `File Type Code`, image/file-icon status text), menu/history summaries (`Numeric shortcuts on/off`, `Menu titles cap at ...`, `Keep the explicit Clear History command visible ...`), shortcuts/update status strings (`Open the full ClipMenu popup at the pointer.`, `Checking for updates...`, `Current version: %@`), and a wider slice of excluded-app / snippet-position / action-summary wording. That still leaves some lower-priority English fallback, but the most visible modern SwiftUI surfaces are materially less mixed-language now.
- A final June 27, 2026 cleanup pass then finished the remaining non-legacy Japanese fallback in the modern Swift surfaces. After adding the last formatted summary/status strings (`%1$@, %2$@, and %3$d more`, `%1$d custom mappings active ...`, `%@ %@ is ready to install`, and `%@ is current`), the same automated scan over `NSLocalizedString` literals in `Source/SwiftUINativeWindows.swift` and `Source/AppController.swift` now reports `missing_ja_non_legacy = 0` while `missing_ja_total = 86`, meaning the remaining misses are confined to legacy object-key lookups such as `1232.title` / `686.title` that resolve through the original `Preferences.strings` tables rather than through untranslated Swift-only copy. `plutil -lint Japanese.lproj/Localizable.strings` and `xcodebuild -project ClipMenu.xcodeproj -scheme ClipMenu -configuration Debug build` both stayed green after that final batch. That materially upgrades the Japanese modern-UI story from "mostly translated" to "all direct Swift-surface copy covered," leaving only the older nib/table-backed localization paths to audit separately.
- A follow-up June 27, 2026 table audit then closed even that last qualifier: extracting every `NSLocalizedString(..., tableName: "Preferences", ...)` key still referenced by the Swift codebase produced exactly `86` legacy object-key lookups, and a direct plist scan confirmed `missing_en = 0` and `missing_ja = 0` across `English.lproj/Preferences.strings` and `Japanese.lproj/Preferences.strings`. In other words, the remaining `missing_ja_total = 86` entries from the literal-string scan are not untranslated runtime gaps at all; they are all satisfied by the inherited nib-era Preferences string tables already shipped in the migrated app. That gives the localization audit a cleaner stopping point: modern Swift-surface copy is fully covered directly, and legacy table-backed copy is also present in both installed languages.

A new Debug-only verifier (`debugWriteMalformedActionsReportAfterLaunchDelay`) now proves that edge case directly against an overridden support directory: with a deliberately invalid `actions.plist` plus a valid fallback `actionMenu.data`, the runtime action loader returned zero top-level nodes, the live action popup menu stayed empty, and the modern Preferences action tree also reloaded to zero nodes (`treatsMalformedPlistAsAuthoritativeEmpty = true`) rather than reviving either the legacy `Legacy Fallback` node or the default `Paste as Plain Text` menu.
